code_hints: If PLP tiles are not found after waiting, treat /men/outerwear as a hub page: querySelectorAll('a[href*="/men/outerwear/"]'). Filter links that include 'down-jackets', 'short-', or 'long-' and navigate to the first match.
Always click the OneTrust cookie acceptor if present (#onetrust-accept-btn-handler) before evaluating the DOM.
After landing on a PLP, scroll incrementally (e.g., 3-5 viewport heights) and wait for network idle to ensure lazy-loaded tiles render before extracting.

PLP extraction: select product anchors with a[href$='.html'][href*='/en-'] and de-duplicate by href. Use the anchor text or aria-label for title when available; price is generally not on PLP, so prioritize PDP extraction.

PDP extraction fallbacks: title from h1[data-testid='product-name'] or h1[itemprop='name']; price from [data-testid='product-price'] or span[itemprop='price']. If still empty, parse application/ld+json for offers.price and name.
Normalization: before queueing links, drop URL fragments and querystrings; keep only https://www.moncler.com/en-gb/... paths.
If redirected away from en-gb locale, rewrite back to en-gb with the same path segments using the url_rules.
rationale: The reported PLP URL (/en-gb/men/outerwear) is a category landing page without product tiles. Moncler’s actual product grids live one level deeper (e.g., /short-down-jackets). We add a rule to auto-drill into a leaf PLP when hitting the hub page, broaden PLP selectors to catch the grid, and add robust PDP title/price fallbacks. We also add OneTrust cookie handling that can block rendering, increase waits for dynamic content, and normalize locale to en-gb to avoid locale traps.
